target: Oes tocyn sbâr gyda ti?
english: Do you have a spare ticket?
tip: Welsh has no verb to have; it uses gyda: Oes tocyn sbâr gyda ti? = literally is there a spare ticket with you?

target: Dyw e erioed wedi bod yn Llundain.
english: He has never been to London.
tip: In a negative, erioed means never in all past time: Dyw e erioed wedi bod = he has never been.

target: Cyfaddefodd e fod e wedi gwneud camgymeriad.
english: He admitted he had made a mistake.
tip: Reported clauses use bod, softened to fod, for that: Cyfaddefodd e fod e wedi gwneud = he admitted that he had made.

target: Mae wedi bod yn bleser cwrdd â chi.
english: It's been a pleasure to meet you.
tip: cwrdd takes â to mean meet with: cwrdd â chi = meet you. â here is with.

target: Mae Owain wedi hedfan i Ddulyn am waith.
english: Owain has flown to Dublin for work.
tip: The preposition i softens the word after it: i Ddulyn (from Dulyn) = to Dublin.

target: Mae'r awyr las yn glir a digymlau heddiw.
english: The blue sky is clear and cloudless today.
tip: A feminine noun softens its adjective: awyr is feminine, so glas becomes awyr las = blue sky.

target: Gwrthodwyd y pryd oherwydd ei fod yn oer.
english: The meal was sent back because it was cold.
tip: The -wyd ending is an agentless passive: Gwrthodwyd y pryd = the meal was sent back, with no doer named.

target: Dw i wedi bod yma o'r blaen, mae'n hyfryd.
english: I've been here before, it's lovely.
tip: o'r blaen means before now and pairs with the perfect: wedi bod yma o'r blaen = have been here before.

target: Mae'r gaeaf yma wedi bod yn fwynach nag arfer.
english: This winter has been milder than usual.
tip: nag means than before a vowel (na before a consonant): yn fwynach nag arfer = milder than usual.

target: Mae e eisoes wedi pacio'i fagiau ar gyfer y daith.
english: He has already packed his bags for the trip.
tip: eisoes means already and sits just before wedi: mae e eisoes wedi pacio = he has already packed.

target: Pe bawn i heb symud yma, fyddwn i byth wedi dysgu Cymraeg.
english: If I hadn't moved here, I'd never have learned Welsh.
tip: heb is the not-done counterpart of wedi: heb symud = not having moved, where wedi symud would mean having moved.

target: Roedd y plant wedi cysgu erbyn wyth o'r gloch.
english: The children had gone to sleep by eight o'clock.
tip: erbyn marks a deadline, not a moment: erbyn wyth o'r gloch = by eight o'clock, meaning done before then.

target: Roedd Trystan wedi byw yng Ngheredigion ers blynyddoedd.
english: Trystan had lived in Ceredigion for years.
tip: The in word yn becomes yng and nasal-mutates a place name: Ceredigion turns into yng Ngheredigion.

target: Methodd e'r ymgais gyntaf ond pasiodd yr ailsefyll.
english: He failed the first attempt but passed the resit.
tip: The -odd ending is the he/she past for one finished event: Methodd = he failed, pasiodd = he passed.

target: Mynd i'r afael â.
english: To get to grips with.
tip: Mynd i'r afael â is a fixed phrase for tackling a task. The â on the end literally means with.

target: Mae cur pen arna i.
english: I have a headache.
tip: Aches and pains take ar (on), not a verb for have. Arna i means on me, so cur pen arna i is a headache on me.

target: Cadwa dy ben yn uchel.
english: Keep your head held high.
tip: dy (your) triggers a soft mutation, so pen (head) becomes ben in dy ben.

target: Mae'r bont dros yr afon.
english: The bridge is over the river.
tip: pont (bridge) is feminine, so it soft-mutates to bont after the article: Mae'r bont.

target: Mae deuddeg mis mewn blwyddyn.
english: There are twelve months in a year.
tip: After a number the noun stays singular: deuddeg mis is twelve month, not months.

target: Mae angen gofalu am ein hiechyd.
english: We need to look after our health.
tip: ein (our) adds an h before a vowel, so iechyd (health) becomes hiechyd in ein hiechyd.

target: Oes beiro neu bensil gyda ti?
english: Do you have a pen or a pencil?
tip: neu (or) triggers a soft mutation, so pensil becomes bensil in neu bensil.

target: Gan fod y llyfrgell ar gau, darllennais yn yr ardd.
english: Since the library was closed, I read in the garden.
tip: Gan fod means because or since. It combines gan with fod, a form of bod (to be).

target: Paratowyd y cinio gan y plant fel syrpreis ar ben-blwydd eu mam.
english: The dinner was prepared by the children as a surprise for their mother's birthday.
tip: The -wyd ending makes a passive, so Paratowyd means was prepared. The doer follows gan (by): gan y plant.

target: Mae gen i ewythr yn Llundain.
english: I have an uncle in London.
tip: Welsh has no verb for have. Mae gen i is literally there is with me, so Mae gen i ewythr is I have an uncle.

target: Heb wybod y gwir, cytunais i.
english: Without knowing the truth, I agreed.
tip: Heb (without) triggers a soft mutation, so gwybod (to know) becomes wybod in Heb wybod.

target: Mae'r cawl cystal â chawl Mam.
english: The soup is as good as Mum's soup.
tip: cystal â means as good as. The â triggers an aspirate mutation, so cawl becomes chawl after it.

target: Edrychwn ymlaen at eich gweld chi eto.
english: We look forward to seeing you again. (formal)
tip: Edrychwn ymlaen at is the set phrase for look forward to. It takes at, not i, before what you await.

target: Mae'r brecwast Cymreig yn cynnwys bara lawr a chig moch.
english: The Welsh breakfast includes laverbread and bacon.
tip: a (and) triggers an aspirate mutation, so cig (meat) becomes chig in a chig moch.

target: Oes awgrymiadau gyda ti?
english: Do you have any suggestions?
tip: Welsh has no verb for have. Possession is shown with gyda: awgrymiadau gyda ti literally means suggestions with you.

target: Gwyddwn i fod e'n dod.
english: I knew he was coming.
tip: To report knew that, Welsh uses fod plus the person: Gwyddwn i fod e'n dod means I knew that he was coming.
